q: What does `nums.insert(0, x)` cost on a Python list of length n?
why: Every existing element shifts one slot right to make room at index 0.

q: What is the time complexity of this function?
why: Each `in` and each `remove` scans or shifts O(n), and it can repeat up to n times. A write pointer does it in one O(n) pass.

q: What does `a` hold after this runs?
why: `nums = ...` only rebinds the local name. To change the caller's list you'd write `nums[:] = [0, 0, 0]`.

q: Rotating an array of length 5 right by k = 12 is the same as rotating it by…
why: Every n rotations bring the array back to the start, so only k % n = 12 % 5 = 2 matters.

q: Merge Sorted Array: why fill nums1 from the back?
options: The free space is at the end, so nothing unread gets overwritten
Python lists can only grow at the end
why: Writing from the front would overwrite values of nums1 you still need. The empty tail is safe to write into.

q: Boyer-Moore voting finds the majority element in…
options: O(n log n) time, O(1) space
why: One pass with just a candidate and a count. It relies on the majority appearing more than n/2 times.
